article.substack_body_markdown:
Retrospective analysis, written on 14 November 2026 (ET)

We think the October NFP report met our frozen Strong condition, while the market response and a separate categorical score answer different questions. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

## What the jobs report resolved

BLS reported October's arrival facts: Payrolls: **+165K** and Unemployment rate: **4.1%**. Capital Chronicle model estimate: that combination met our frozen Strong condition. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_6]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_7]]

The Bureau of Labor Statistics published its October employment release at 8:30 a.m. ET on November 6, 2026. BLS described gains in professional and business services, health care, and transportation and warehousing. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_6]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_7]]

BLS also reported average hourly earnings increased 0.4 percent in October. September's payroll gain was revised from +29,000 to +60,000 in this release. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_6]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_7]]

Our history panels retain the dated first releases before October; September's original print remains distinct from its later revision. Gaps remain unfilled in the historical panels. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_6]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_7]]

The industry bars separate mining and logging, construction, manufacturing and private services. They show selected, disjoint employment groups, not a complete jobs total or sector investment returns. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_6]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_7]]

## Scenarios

Capital Chronicle model estimate: our frozen Strong condition required payrolls about +154K or more and unemployment 4.2% or lower. Both conditions held, so this release matched Strong. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

The frozen Weak alternative required payrolls about -24K or lower and unemployment 4.2% or higher. That combination did not hold. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Our frozen Strong mechanism was that a hawkish labour surprise would raise the expected Fed path, the dollar and real yields. The Weak countercase was that another weak print would lower the expected hike path and weaken the dollar. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

## What moved, and when

Capital Chronicle model estimate: our earliest measured window is five minutes after the 8:30 a.m. ET release. The later observation is sixty minutes after the same baseline. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

These windows do not identify which market moved first within the opening minutes. Our frozen EUR/USD context placed price low in a five-week 1.1104-1.1286 range; the observed changes alone do not establish a range break. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

The measured changes are reference-series co-movements, not causal attribution or measured futures or ETF returns. We have no completed first-day observation. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]][[SOURCE:SOURCE_2]]

### Rates

We lack a matched bond-yield observation, so we cannot test the expected real-yield leg. That part of the frozen mechanism remains untested here. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

### Dollar

Capital Chronicle model estimate: the EUR/USD reference changed -0.0555% after five minutes and -0.2723% after sixty minutes. The USD/JPY reference changed 0.0152% and 0.0429% over those respective windows. These are not FXE or FXY ETF returns; FXY expresses yen versus dollars, the inverse quotation direction to USD/JPY. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

### Gold

Capital Chronicle model estimate: the gold reference changed -0.2335% after five minutes and -0.6723% after sixty minutes. These are reference changes, not GC gold futures returns or proof that the release caused them. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

### Oil

Capital Chronicle model estimate: the WTI reference initially rose 0.228%, then stood -0.1813% from the baseline after sixty minutes. Its reversal challenges a uniform-response story; these are not CL WTI futures returns. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

### Equities

Capital Chronicle model estimate: the S&P 500 reference changed -0.0423% after five minutes and -0.0949% after sixty minutes. These are reference observations, not ES futures or SPY ETF returns. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

### Sectors

The industry bars measure employment changes. Without matched sector-return observations, we make no sector-performance claim. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_3]]

## What the separate score tells us

In the separate historical-frequency comparison, the Capital Chronicle model estimate classified the outcome as in line and assigned the matrix a Brier score of 0.02. Lower is better. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

This is one event and a different comparison from the preview's Strong and Weak conditions. The in-line category does not reverse which frozen release condition was met or establish predictive skill. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

For that same event, the Capital Chronicle model estimate gave Investing's consensus-only baseline a Brier score of 0. The consensus baseline therefore performed better on this categorical metric. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

We cannot count the Strong resolution and the in-line category as independent successes. Neither result supplies a second independent event or a performance record. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

No prediction-market-only score is available for this event, so we cannot assess that baseline. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

## The lesson

Our interpretation is that the dollar and gold co-movements are consistent with the frozen hawkish mechanism. The countercase is that consistency does not establish causation, especially without a matched rates observation. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

What we cannot claim is predictive skill: the consensus-only categorical baseline scored better, and the missing rates and first-day observations leave parts of the mechanism untested. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

So what: judge the release condition, observed response and forecast baseline separately; agreement between them cannot establish predictive skill. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

For the next review, we would preserve the frozen conditions and compare fully dated market observations against a baseline before claiming that a mechanism worked. This retrospective provides no current market guidance. Our dated analysis does not independently confirm events or establish a performance record. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]

Capital Chronicle offers analysis only, not financial advice or recommendations. [[SOURCE:SOURCE_1]]
